query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve hardness and strength without sacrificing useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the mechanism expected to produce the improvement, a measurable outcome relative to an untreated baseline, the conditions under which the hypothesis should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment with clear observations that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of coherent nanoprecipitations in refractory high-entropy alloys can improve their hardness and strength without sacrificing useful mechanical performance.
generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloys in their as-cast or as-fabricated state
generation.intervention: Introduction of coherent nanoprecipitations through a controlled process
generation.conditions: Ambient temperature and high-temperature conditions up to 800 °C
generation.structural_mediator: Coherent nanoprecipitations with a body-centered cubic structure
generation.mechanism: Dislocation transmission and relief of stress concentrations through the coherent interfaces of nanoprecipitations
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved hardness and strength without compromising tensile ductility
generation.baseline: Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys with no nanoprecipitations
generation.boundary: Temperature range up to 800 °C and strain rates relevant to high-temperature applications
generation.uncertainty: The exact composition and processing conditions required to achieve optimal nanoprecipitation morphology and distribution

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of mechanical properties between refractory high-entropy alloys with and without coherent nanoprecipitations
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of coherent nanoprecipitations does not result in improved hardness and strength without sacrificing tensile ductility, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract High-performance refractory alloys with ultrahigh strength and ductility are in demand for a wide range of critical applications, such as plasma-facing components. However, it remains challenging to increase the strength of these alloys without seriously compromising their tensile ductility. Here, we put forward a strategy to “defeat” this trade-off in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys by stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs). The coherent interfaces of SCCPs facilitate the dislocation transmission and relieve the stress concentrations that can lead to premature crack initiation. As a consequence, our alloy displays an ultrahigh strength of 2.15 GPa with a tensile ductility of 15% at ambient temperature, with a high yield strength of 1.05 GPa at 800 °C. The SCCPs design concept may afford a means to develop a wide range of ultrahigh-strength metallic materials by providing a pathway for alloy design. Subject terms: Metals and alloys, Mechanical engineering

Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) have excellent mechanical properties, which could make them the substitutes of some superalloys. However, the high melting point of refractory HEAs leads to processing problems when using traditional processing techniques. In this study, a single BCC solid solution of NbMoTaW alloy was formed by selective laser melting (SLM) with a linear energy density of up to 2.83 J/mm. The composition distribution was analyzed, and the element with a lower melting point and lower density showed a negative deviation (no more than 5%) of the molar ratio in the formed alloy. The HEA shows an excellent microstructure, microhardness, and corrosion resistance performance compared with traditional superalloys, making it a new substitute metal with great application prospects in aerospace and energy fields.
